meta.titre: Company Formation Documents: who needs which paper and when
meta.sous_theme: Memorandum, articles, certificates, prospectus and dividend calculations

sections.contenu_markdown: Three friends who run a small trading business decide to turn it into a company, so that the business becomes a separate legal person and their own property is protected if it fails. Before the company can trade, certain papers must be drawn up and registered, and some of them must be shown to the public. The GCE Commerce papers ask which document contains what, which one gives the company legal existence and which one allows a public company to begin work. This course sets the documents out in the order in which they appear.

items: A company is owned by shareholders, who hold shares in it.
Limited liability means that shareholders can lose no more than the amount they invested.
A dividend is the part of the profit paid out to shareholders.
A private company does not offer its shares to the public; a public limited company may do so.

sections.titre: The documents needed to form a company
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Incorporation

**Incorporation** means registering a business as a company with the registrar of companies. The company then becomes a legal person, separate from its owners, able to own property, sign contracts and sue or be sued in its own name.

### The documents

| Document | What it contains or does |
|---|---|
| **Memorandum of association** | The company's relations with the outside world: its name, the address of its registered office, its objects (the business it may carry on), the liability of its members and its authorised share capital |
| **Articles of association** | The internal rules: rights of shareholders, how shares are issued and transferred, how directors are appointed and what powers they have, how meetings are held and voted, and how profits are shared as dividends |
| **Certificate of incorporation** | Issued by the registrar once the documents are accepted; proof that the company legally exists. A private company may begin to trade when it receives it |
| **Prospectus** | Issued by a public limited company to invite the public to buy its shares; it gives details of the company, its directors and how to apply |
| **Certificate of trading** (certificate to commence business) | Issued to a public limited company once it has raised the minimum share capital; the company may not start business without it |

### The order of events

Memorandum and articles are drawn up and registered, then the certificate of incorporation is issued. A private company can start trading. A public limited company issues its prospectus, raises its capital and only then obtains its certificate of trading. Textbooks differ slightly in the names they use, so follow the terms taught in your course.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks which documents a particular type of company needs
variantes.contenu_markdown: A **private company** needs the memorandum, the articles and the certificate of incorporation. A **public limited company** needs the same documents, and also a prospectus (to invite the public to subscribe) and a certificate of trading before it begins business.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the business is a partnership and not a company
variantes.contenu_markdown: A partnership is not incorporated, so it has no certificate of incorporation. Its partners usually sign a **partnership deed** (agreement) that states the capital each puts in, how profits and losses are shared, and the rules for running the firm. For a company, the sharing of profits is written in the articles of association.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When numbers of shares, capital or dividends must be calculated
variantes.contenu_markdown: $\text{Share capital} = \text{number of shares} \times \text{nominal value of one share}$. Authorised capital uses the shares the company is allowed to issue; issued capital uses the shares actually issued. Total dividend $= \text{dividend per share} \times \text{shares issued}$; a shareholder receives the dividend per share times the shares he holds.

sections.enonce_markdown: A public limited company is allowed to issue 400,000 shares of 500 FCFA each and has issued 300,000 of them. (a) List, in order, the documents it needs before it can trade. (b) Calculate the authorised and the issued capital. (c) The directors declare a dividend of 45 FCFA per share out of a profit of 18,000,000 FCFA available for distribution (hypothetical figures). Calculate the total dividend, the profit kept in the business and the dividend of a shareholder who holds 2,000 shares.

etapes.justification: A public limited company must be incorporated, must invite the public to subscribe and must be allowed to start business.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Memorandum and articles of association, certificate of incorporation, prospectus, certificate of trading

etapes.justification: Authorised capital uses all the shares the company may issue.
Issued capital uses the shares actually issued.

etapes.action: Calculate the total dividend and the retained profit
etapes.justification: The dividend per share is multiplied by the shares issued; the rest of the profit stays in the business.
Multiply the dividend per share by the shares held.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Authorised capital is 200,000,000 FCFA and issued capital is 150,000,000 FCFA. The total dividend is 13,500,000 FCFA, 4,500,000 FCFA of profit is kept, and the shareholder receives 90,000 FCFA.** The company may begin business only after it has received the certificate of trading.

items.erreur_markdown: 'The memorandum of association contains the internal rules of the company.'
items.pourquoi_faux: The internal rules are in the articles. The memorandum deals with the company's relations with outsiders.
items.correction_markdown: Memorandum: name, registered office, objects, liability, authorised capital. Articles: internal rules such as directors' powers and profit sharing.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A public limited company can start trading as soon as it has its certificate of incorporation.'
items.pourquoi_faux: That is true of a private company. A public limited company also needs a certificate of trading.
items.correction_markdown: Public limited company: certificate of incorporation, then prospectus and capital raised, then certificate of trading.

items.erreur_markdown: 'A private company issues a prospectus to the public to sell its shares.'
items.pourquoi_faux: A private company does not offer its shares to the public. The prospectus belongs to a public limited company.
items.correction_markdown: Only a public limited company invites the public to buy shares by a prospectus.

items.pourquoi_faux: The company itself issues the prospectus. The registrar issues the certificates.
items.correction_markdown: Company: prospectus. Registrar: certificate of incorporation and certificate of trading.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that a company's profits are shared according to the partnership deed
items.pourquoi_faux: A partnership deed belongs to partnerships. In a company the articles set out how profits are shared.
items.correction_markdown: Partnership: partnership deed. Incorporated company: articles of association.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the document: (a) it states the name and objects of a company; (b) it sets out how directors are appointed and how meetings are held; (c) it proves that a company legally exists; (d) it invites the public to buy shares in a company.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Memorandum of association**. (b) **Articles of association**. (c) **Certificate of incorporation**. (d) **Prospectus**.

items.enonce_markdown: A private company may issue 50,000 shares of 1,000 FCFA each and has issued 32,000. Calculate the authorised capital, the issued capital and the value of the shares not yet issued. A dividend of 60 FCFA per share is declared: calculate the total dividend.
items.solution_markdown:
Authorised capital $= 50\,000 \times 1\,000 = 50\,000\,000$ FCFA.

Issued capital $= 32\,000 \times 1\,000 = 32\,000\,000$ FCFA.

Shares not yet issued: $50\,000 - 32\,000 = 18\,000$ shares, worth $18\,000\,000$ FCFA.

Total dividend $= 60 \times 32\,000 = 1\,920\,000$ FCFA.

**Authorised: 50,000,000 FCFA; issued: 32,000,000 FCFA; unissued: 18,000,000 FCFA; dividend: 1,920,000 FCFA.**

items.enonce_markdown: The articles of a company say that ordinary shareholders receive a dividend of 10% of the nominal value of their shares. There are 120,000 ordinary shares of 1,000 FCFA each, and the profit available for distribution is 20,000,000 FCFA (hypothetical figures). (a) Name the document that sets the rule for sharing profits. (b) Calculate the dividend per share and the total dividend. (c) Calculate the profit kept in the business. (d) Calculate the dividend of a shareholder who holds 1,500 shares. (e) Explain why a public limited company needs two certificates before it can trade.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The **articles of association**.

(b) Dividend per share $= 10\% \times 1\,000 = 100$ FCFA. Total dividend $= 100 \times 120\,000 = 12\,000\,000$ FCFA.

(c) Profit kept $= 20\,000\,000 - 12\,000\,000 = 8\,000\,000$ FCFA.

(d) Shareholder: $1\,500 \times 100 = 150\,000$ FCFA.

(e) The certificate of incorporation gives the company legal existence. A public limited company also raises money from the public, so it needs the certificate of trading to show that the minimum capital has been raised before it begins business.

**Dividend per share: 100 FCFA; total dividend: 12,000,000 FCFA; profit kept: 8,000,000 FCFA; shareholder: 150,000 FCFA.**

items_markdown: Incorporation makes a company a legal person separate from its owners.
Memorandum of association: name, registered office, objects, liability and authorised capital; it deals with the outside world.
Articles of association: internal rules, including the powers of directors and the sharing of profits as dividends.
Certificate of incorporation: proof that the company exists; a private company can trade once it has it.
A public limited company also issues a prospectus and must obtain a certificate of trading before it begins business.
Share capital = number of shares × nominal value; total dividend = dividend per share × shares issued.
